use_case_requirements: Primary workloads: (1) internal-facing agent assist for support reps, (2) customer correspondence summarization, (3) embeddings-based doc search across policy/procedure corpus. They expect spiky traffic during market hours and month-end. Wants predictable spend and the ability to reconcile invoice line items to internal cost centers.
technical_notes: Latency: target <800ms time-to-first-token for agent assist in-region; throughput bursts acceptable with autoscaling but prefers reserved capacity for predictable performance. Model flexibility is secondary to compliance; open to Redwood-recommended models if we can pin versions and support controlled rollouts. Requires usage exports (daily) for internal chargeback; expects consistent timezone handling and stable schemas.
security_retention_notes: Top concerns are metering/billing data handling and access. Contoso’s policy: do not retain customer content (prompts/completions) outside their boundary; they are willing to allow retention of strictly necessary billing telemetry (aggregated token counts, request counts, model/region, timestamps) with documented purpose limitation. They asked: (a) default retention for raw request logs vs usage events vs billing ledger, (b) ability to configure retention shorter for raw logs while keeping ledger/audit artifacts longer, (c) whether Redwood can provide immutable audit logs for access to billing datasets and exports, and (d) who at Redwood can access metering data (role-based access, approval workflow, and logging). They also requested SSO/SAML enforcement for Console and least-privileged roles for Finance/RevOps access.
metering_data_access_constraints: Contoso is restricting what Redwood can store and who can query it. They prefer: (1) no prompt/completion content stored; (2) usage events contain only metering dimensions (account_id, project_id, model, region, billed_tokens, cache_hit attribution, request_id/idempotency key) with redacted identifiers where possible; (3) customer-facing usage export must be sufficient for invoice reconciliation without Redwood exposing raw logs; (4) any backfills or meter definition changes must be auditable and communicated (they asked specifically about ‘shadow billing compare’ to prevent invoice surprises). They want an explicit statement that late-arriving events/backfills will not retroactively change invoiced amounts without formal approval/notice.
open_questions: 1) Can we support Contoso requirement to disable retention of request payloads entirely while keeping metering correctness (esp. for retries/streaming)? 2) What is the minimum retention period we require for dispute resolution and how does that align with Contoso retention controls? 3) How do we present ‘billed tokens vs raw tokens’ and cache-hit attribution in a way their auditors accept? 4) Confirm whether all billing-related access is centrally logged and exportable for their compliance team.
